notes:
Alaska's recurring entity-level levy on an LLC is the Business License of AS 43.70, administered by the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing of the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development. AS 43.70.020(a) requires the license "for the privilege of engaging in a business in the state" and AS 43.70.030(a) sets the fee at $50 a year, with reduced rates reserved for sole proprietors who are seniors or disabled veterans. The renewal application (form 08-4617, rev. 10/01/2025) sells one- or two-year terms for $50 or $100, both ending December 31; minimumAnnualUsd carries the $50 annual floor and dueDate carries the form's own license-term line.
The record treats the Business License as the franchise-type levy on substance, the same call Nevada's State Business License made: it is a recurring, state-level charge on the privilege of doing business, owed for as long as the entity operates, whatever the state calls it. collectedWithAnnualReport is false: root states.json carries annual_report_fee 100 for Alaska, the biennial report fee paid to the Corporations Section of the same division, a separate payment with no overlap.
firstYearExemption is false on the statute's own terms: a person must apply, obtain the license and pay the fee before first engaging in business, and no first-year waiver is stated.
stateIncomeTax: Alaska has no individual income tax. The Department of Revenue's own Personal Income program page says so in terms, so passThroughApplies is false, topRatePercent is null and hasPTETElection is false; there is no income tax for an entity-level election to elect into. The Department's programs list also names Corporate Income Tax, which reaches corporations and is out of scope for a default LLC.
The Business Licensing portal (commerce.alaska.gov) serves a JavaScript challenge to scripted clients on this route, so the division's FAQ pages were not read; the statute and the official renewal form carry every recorded value.
